title: Trace function of the Artin–Schreier sheaf
statement:
Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, fix the nondegenerate additive character
$\psi=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}$ of [def-fd-additive-character],
let $a\in k_0^\times$, and let $\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$ be the
Artin–Schreier sheaf of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] on
$\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ attached to the linear function $x\mapsto ax$.
Then the *trace function* of $\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$ is

$$
t_{\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}}(u)=\psi\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/k_0}(au)\bigr)
=\Psi\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/\mathbf F_p}(au)\bigr),
$$

for every closed point $u$ (with the local Frobenius convention of
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]); in particular, on the
$\mathbf F_{q^n}$-points of the line,

$$
t_{\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}}(x)=\psi\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{q^n}/k_0}(ax)\bigr).
$$

proof.text: Work with the current $\mathrm{AS}_q$ definition, as stated literally in [sk-def-as], and the rational adic coefficient convention [sk-def-fourier-set]. Choose its finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ containing $\mu_p$, so that $\psi$ is $E$-valued. On $A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ let $\pi_0:\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\to A_0$ be $y\mapsto y^q-y$. Clause 1 of [lem-a1-artin-schreier-trace-cover-map], with $X=A_0$, $f=x$ and auxiliary $b=1$, says that $\pi_0$ is finite etale and its geometric fibres are $k_0$-torsors under translation. Let $M_E=R\pi_*E$ on the geometric line, where $E$ has its canonical Weil structure [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. The finite adic direct-image theorem [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] makes $M_E$ a constructible sheaf in degree zero. The direct-image and automorphism equivariance of [lem-fix-weil-operations] equip it with a Weil isomorphism and make every translation $\sigma_c^*$ an equivariant endomorphism. All operations here take place in $D^b_c(-,E)$; $E$ is a rational coefficient field, not a torsion coefficient ring.

proof.text: In the constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart] take the idempotent $e_\psi=q^{-1}\sum_{c\in k_0}\psi(-c)\sigma_c^*$ of [sk-def-as]. By [prop-weil-heart-abelian] it splits; put $N_E=\operatorname{im}e_\psi$. Equivariance of each translation implies $e_\psi\theta=\theta\,g^*e_\psi$, so restricting $\theta$ and its inverse to the image gives an invertible Weil map on $N_E$. For the $k_0$-isomorphism $m_a:x\mapsto ax$ put $K_E=Lm_a^*N_E$ with the pullback Weil structure of [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Pullback is exact on the constructible heart and on point fibres by [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact], so $K_E$ is again a sheaf and its stalk is the image of the pulled-back projector. This is precisely the $E$-model of $\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$: [sk-def-as] defines $\mathcal L_\psi$ by this projector on $(\mathrm{AS}_q)_*E$ and defines $\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}=m_a^*\mathcal L_\psi$. This is also the current blueprint_update of def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf. No identification of a degree-$q$ cover with a degree-$p$ cover is made.

proof.text: Let $n\ge1$, let $u\in A_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and put $b=au$, so $m_a\bar u=\bar z$ is the point $x=b$. Pullback composition [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], rationalized as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], identifies the point complex of $Lm_a^*M_E$ at $\bar u$ with that of $M_E$ at $\bar z$. By [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] the latter is $E^{P}$ in degree zero, $P$ the geometric points $\bar y$ of the cover over $\bar z$, identified by their coordinate $y(\bar y)$ with $S_b=\{y\in k:y^q-y=b\}$; translation acts as $(\sigma_c^*h)(y)=h(y+c)$. Evaluate the composite defining $F_u^{(n)}$ in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], where $\gamma=\varphi_q^{-1}$ and $g$ is $g_Y$ on the cover. By the stated naturality of [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] in semilinear isomorphisms, the point transport [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] sends $h$ to $h'$ with $h'(\bar y g_s^n)=h(\bar y)$; the direct-image Weil map, followed by the canonical constant map [def-weil-constant-weil-structure], which keeps values in $E$, sends $h'$ to $\bar y\mapsto h'(g^n\bar y)$. So $F_u^{(n)}h(\bar y)=h(\bar y')$ with $\bar y'g_s^n=g^n\bar y$. On the coordinate ring of the cover both ring maps send $c\mapsto\gamma^n(c)$, and $y$ to $\gamma^n(y(\bar y'))$, resp. $y(\bar y)$; hence $y(\bar y')=y(\bar y)^{q^n}$ and the composite is $h\mapsto(y\mapsto h(y^{q^n}))$. The return holds since $b\in\mathbf F_{q^n}$, and $m_a$ is defined over $k_0$, so it commutes with $g$. Naturality of point transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] carries the projector through this composite, so the local operator of $K_E$ is the restriction of this operator to $e_\psi E^{S_b}$.

proof.text: The equation $y^q=y+b$ gives, by induction, $y^{q^j}=y+\sum_{i<j}b^{q^i}$: raise the formula to the $q$-th power and substitute $y^q=y+b$. By [lem-a1-finite-field-trace-frobenius-sum] for $k_0\subset\mathbf F_{q^n}$, put $t=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{q^n}/k_0}(b)=\sum_{i<n}b^{q^i}\in k_0$. Hence $y^{q^n}=y+t$, and the operator in step 3 is exactly $\sigma_t^*$. The $\psi$-isotypic space of [sk-def-as] is one-dimensional: choose $y_0\in S_b$; the torsor assertion of [lem-a1-artin-schreier-trace-cover-map](1) gives $S_b=y_0+k_0$. A $\psi$-eigenfunction must satisfy $h(y_0+c)=\psi(c)h(y_0)$, so evaluation at $y_0$ identifies this space with $E$; conversely this formula defines an eigenfunction for every value in $E$. On it $\sigma_t^*$ is multiplication by $\psi(t)$. Its ordinary trace is consequently $\psi(t)$, with no higher-degree contribution.

proof.text: Pass from the constructed $E$-Weil pair $K_E=(M,\theta)$ to the framework $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-pair $((E,M),[E,\theta])$ exactly as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex](4), including the inverse $[E,\theta^{-1}]$. For $X=\mathbf A^1_k$, the equivalence $J_X$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] sends this to the PBC pair whose underlying object is $(E,J_{X,E}M)$ and whose Weil isomorphism is the composite $Lg_X^{*,\mathrm{pbc}}J_X(E,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_XLg_X^{*,\mathrm{sf}}(E,M)\xrightarrow{J_X[E,\theta]}J_X(E,M)$. The first arrow is the inverse of that lemma's specified Frobenius comparison; its finite-stage compatibility ensures this is the entire pair corresponding to $K_E$. The hypotheses hold: the geometric affine line is noetherian, of dimension one, and $\ell$ is invertible. By the prescription of [def-fd-trace-function], evaluate this PBC pair by the corresponding framework pair and its model $K_E$, taking the finite alternating trace in $E$ and including it into $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Step 4 therefore gives $t_{\mathcal L_{\psi,ax},n}(u)=\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{q^n}/k_0}(au))$. This passage retains the Weil map, rather than identifying the coefficient categories just by their underlying objects.

proof.text: For a closed point $u$ of degree $n$, choose its residue-field embedding in $k$ and apply the preceding calculation with $\mathbf F_{q^n}=\kappa(u)$; its local operator is precisely $F_u$ by [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. To verify the second equality without an uncited trace-transitivity theorem, write $q=p^r$ and $b=au$. Apply [lem-a1-finite-field-trace-frobenius-sum] to $k_0/\mathbf F_p$, $\kappa(u)/k_0$ and $\kappa(u)/\mathbf F_p$. In $\kappa(u)$ this gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/k_0}(b))=\sum_{i<r}(\sum_{j<n}b^{p^{rj}})^{p^i}=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<r}b^{p^{rj+i}}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/\mathbf F_p}(b)$. The middle equality uses additivity of Frobenius in characteristic $p$ and the bijection $(j,i)\mapsto rj+i$ onto $\{0,\ldots,rn-1\}$. Since $\psi=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}$ by [def-fd-additive-character], applying $\Psi$ gives the second displayed equality. Steps 3–5 already apply to every $\mathbf F_{q^n}$-rational point, even one whose closed-point degree is a proper divisor of $n$, and give the final asserted formula with the $n$-fold local operator.
